title: Developer Adoption Quickplays: Mini Binder (draft)
content:
Purpose:
A compact, slide-sized set of plays and a battlecard for SDR/SE/SEPs to land developer-led pilots and small platform integrations. Focus: 10–25 engineer pilot, move to reserved capacity conversation.

Audience:
- Integration / Platform engineers
- Head of Infrastructure / Platform
- ML Engineers responsible for inference cost and latency

Topline TL;DR (elevator):
- Ship LLM features quickly with predictable performance.
- Start hosted -> reserve Dedicated after 2x throughput or strict latency need.
- Typical pilot: 2 weeks integration, 4–8M tokens/month to validate.

Slide 1: Opening pitch (30s)
- Problem: unpredictable token costs, variable tail latency, and ops overhead when you DIY.
- Redwood value: consistent latency SLOs, cost levers (batching, quantization), and safe fallback routing.
- One-liner ask: 2-week pilot, devs onboard, limited data -> ROI readout.

Slide 2: Developer quick checklist (what devs want)
- Minimal SDK changes: show snippet (pseudo-code) -> 3 lines to change endpoint.
- Prebuilt model templates for chat/generation/embeddings.
- Local debugging with request replay and KV cache inspector.
- Canary steps: staged traffic, automatic fallback to smaller model.

Slide 3: Tech proof points (bite-sized)
- Latency: median <40ms for small generative workloads on Dedicated; sample benchmark ID: BENCH-2025-02-A
- Cost: batching & kv cache typically reduce per-token cost 20–40% for chat sessions (example numbers included in appendix).
- Reliability: built-in routing across zones + canary auto-fallback.

Battlecard snippets (one-pagers for quick reference)
- Objection: "We can run this ourselves on our infra" -> Reply: Yes, but ops timeline and TCO: 3–6 months + ongoing patching. Ask: how many SRE/infra hours/month will inference consume? (use our TCO template).
- Objection: "Vendor lock/security" -> Reply: Private deployment option (VPC or on-prem) + KMS integration + audit logs. Offer: architecture sketch and compliance checklist within 48h.
- Objection: "Cost" -> Reply: show per-route unit economics, propose pilot cap & automated cold-start savings.

Pilot activation script (SE playbook)
1) Kickoff: 30-min tech sync (collect seq length distribution, qps, payload size).
2) 48h onboarding: sample app + skeleton config + canary route.
3) Week 1: measure latency tail, token cost per convo, enable KV cache if chat-heavy.
4) Week 2: run stress test (2x expected qps) and decision point: continue hosted or convert to Dedicated trial.

Success metrics (for buyer)
- P99 latency within X ms target (customer-defined)
- Per-conversation token cost reduced or predictable within ±10%
- Integration dev time <2 weeks
- Customer-run demo showing A/B quality parity with their baseline

Quick rebuttal cheats (fast lines)
- "We already use X provider" -> "We can interop as fallback; our routing can reduce your spend without retraining flows."
- "We need file-based or long-context apps" -> "We support prefix/KV caching and chunking patterns; sample configs available."

Pricing anchors to use in conversation
- Pilot (hosted): capped monthly consumption + free dev seats for first month.
- Dedicated: commit tiers with burst allowance; include SLA pads for p99 latency.
- Private: platform fee + support tier + optional on-prem packaging.

Appendix / Speaker notes (for SE)
- Demo script: 1) run small chat app -> show latency stream; 2) enable batching and show cost delta; 3) flip to fallbacks and show uninterrupted service.
- Key logs to surface: per-route token breakdown, KV cache hit rate, model-variant fallback counts.

Open questions / TODOs
- Need a short, copyable config snippet for embedding pipelines (Priya to draft).
- Collect two concrete customer examples with token numbers for the pricing slide (Diego owning).
- Confirm benchmark IDs and update appendix with raw numbers (bench team).

Notes to self: keep this compact — sellers want 1–2 slides + one pager. This mini-binder is intended to be copy-pasted into a 3-slide deck for meetings.

Contacts / owners
